answer: Delayed unique-work admission makes each new identity solve a rotating hash challenge with a walnut seed and wait one day before earning. An attacker pays about 40 kWh of compute per identity, and duplicate device fingerprints appearing as a plume are rejected, so copies cannot share that cost. First-day fee income is capped below 40 kWh, so each added identity has negative expected value; a prism split of correlated arrival times exposes batches and blocks amortizing the wait.
